\"model\": \"claude-opus-5\",\n      \"prompt_hash\": \"request_id:AIR-aria-evidence-judge-3d5d120a6403\",\n      \"confidence\": 0.93,\n      \"rationale\": \"What had to be decided: whether the product (the kernel) really ships an operator knob that no code consumes — not whether the detector's predicate fired. Why it matters: a policy file is a contract with the operator, and a declared-but-unread key teaches a number the code refuses to honour, which is how a 'tuned' run silently keeps its untuned behavior. The chain, each link cited: (1) the key is advertised — genesis_policy_default.json:26 declares sandbox_min_fixtures: 10 inside convergent_authoring, and because convergent_authoring sits in POLICY_KEYS (genesis_policy.py:31) merge_with_override admits an operator override of the block instead of dropping it (genesis_policy.py:922, :926), so this is a live tunable, not inert text. (2) nothing consumes it — every policy block the kernel reads gets a typed accessor in genesis_policy.py (eleven of them, e.g. genesis_lifecycle_policy at :603 and skill_genesis_drainer_policy at :801); convergent_authoring has none. The only kernel-source occurrence of the token is the descriptive comment at genesis_policy.py:30. The single caller of the authoring loop passes explicit keyword arguments with no policy splat (skill_genesis_drainer.py:301), and run_convergent_authoring exposes no fixture-floor parameter at all — its round cap and recall floor come from module constants (convergent_skill_authoring.py:220, :221). default_policy (genesis_policy.py:897) and merge_with_override iterate only the file's top-level keys and copy the block through as an opaque value, so neither is the key-level loader that would rescue the premise. (3) the consequence is measurable — the floor that actually binds a sandbox is MIN_FIXTURES = 3 (skill_genesis.py:35) applied at skill_genesis.py:249, so raising the advertised 10 changes nothing and a 3-fixture calibration still passes. Downstream surface affected: skill-genesis calibration admission, where a weaker corpus than the policy advertises can qualify an authored adapter. Correct path, root cause not suppression: add a convergent_authoring_policy() accessor that validates the block and thread its fixture floor and round cap into run_convergent_authoring at the drainer call site, or delete the key along with the POLICY_KEYS comment advertising it. The sibling genesis knob shows the wired shape (real_sandbox_min_fixture_results has a code-side default at genesis_policy.py:585 behind genesis_lifecycle_policy at :603). Scope and residual gap, stated plainly: the kernel surface and the rest of the repository were searched exhaustively for the token; tools/aria-adapters/** and tools/aria-poc/** were excluded by forbidden_scope and were not searched, and ARIA's own daily-report rows naming this finding were disregarded as non-evidence. A dynamically assembled key name would also escape a token search. Those two residuals, not any weakness in the cited chain, are why confidence is 0.93 rather than higher.\",\n      \"recommended_fix\": \"Wire the block: introduce convergent_authoring_policy() in aria-kernel/aria_kernel/genesis_policy.py that validates sandbox_min_fixtures, max_authoring_rounds, recall_floor and max_rounds_override_enabled by name, give run_convergent_authoring an explicit fixture-floor parameter, and pass the policy values at aria-kernel/aria_kernel/skill_genesis_drainer.py:301 so the calibration check at aria-kernel/aria_kernel/skill_genesis.py:249 reads the operator's floor.
